referred_to_by.content: A Metaconceptual Art work that Sun & Rain Works designates around its consignment of the Ansel Adams photograph 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks' (lot 16) to Sotheby's Photographs, 2009 (sale N08533, New York). Titled as a play on the auction and the canonical name of Ansel Adams, it treats the act of bringing the photograph to auction — its lot, its authority, its attribution — as the material of a conceptual work, alongside the born-digital work www.wtfisart.com. The work is a designation asserted by the artist and made explicit over time; it is not recorded as a publicly witnessed performance, and the Sotheby's catalogue lists the lot as an Ansel Adams photograph without naming Sun & Rain Works.

Documentation reported by Sun & Rain Works includes 2008 correspondence with Sotheby's Photographs, the public catalogue lot, photographs, and related records; these evidence the artist identity and the consignment. The fuller archive remains held by the studio pending redaction and rights review. This record asserts no historical-priority or precedence claim absent separately published evidence.

referred_to_by.content: What the W stands for, in the artist's account. The studio states, in 2026, that the W of this title stands for 'Who', so that it reads 'Who the F is Ansel Adams', while the W of the companion work www.wtfisart.com stands for 'What'. No document from 2008 or 2009 spells out either expansion; this collection searched the correspondence of those years and the studio's working files and found none. The reading is the artist's and is recorded as that. What the choice does can be stated without adding to it: 'What' is the ordinary word of the idiom, so the companion work asks what art is, and 'Who' bends the idiom, so this work asks instead about a person - who the photographer is, and so what his name, stamp and signature do to a print whose identity rests on them. That gloss is this collection's and not the artist's.

A work in its own right. Earlier versions of this record modelled WTF is Ansel Adams as a part of a titled work, 'The Auction as Artwork'. There was no such titled work; that phrase names the concept the studio's two works around the 2009 engagement share, and the correction is set out in the record for that concept. This work is recorded as a work, related to www.wtfisart.com, and its making is recorded as influenced by the concept rather than as a part of it. The origin claim for 2009 names www.wtfisart.com as its work and this one as the related work, because the website's name is independently dated and this work's title is not: the only public use of the title held here is an undated profile biography.
